/-!
# Conjecture 5.48

by V. N. Remeslennikov

Suppose that $G$ and $H$ are finitely generated residually finite groups having the same set
of finite homomorphic images. Are $G$ and $H$ isomorphic if one of them is a free
(free soluble) group?

Two finitely generated groups have the same set of finite homomorphic images (up to
isomorphism) if and only if their profinite completions are isomorphic, so the free case asks
whether finitely generated free groups are *profinitely rigid* among finitely generated
residually finite groups. The parenthetical question asks the same with "free" replaced by
"free soluble", i.e. free in the variety of soluble groups of derived length at most $d$
for some $d$.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

def IsResiduallyFinite (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ g : G, g ≠ 1 → ∃ N : Subgroup G, N.Normal ∧ N.FiniteIndex ∧ g ∉ N
blocks.docstring:
A group $G$ is *residually finite* if every non-identity element of $G$ lies outside
some normal subgroup of finite index; equivalently, every non-identity element has a
non-identity image in some finite homomorphic image of $G$.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Mathlib has Subgroup.FiniteIndex and Subgroup.Normal but no residual-finiteness predicate; grepped Mathlib and the repo for 'residually', 'ResiduallyFinite', 'profinite completion' with no hits.
justification.name: Kourovka.«5.48».IsResiduallyFinite
justification.why_needed: Residual finiteness of a group is not in Mathlib or FormalConjecturesForMathlib (only mentioned in a Mathlib doc comment). Defined as: every g ≠ 1 lies outside some normal subgroup of finite index (Subgroup.Normal ∧ Subgroup.FiniteIndex), the standard definition.

blocks.name: IsResiduallyFinite
blocks.text:
/-- A group $G$ is *residually finite* if every non-identity element of $G$ lies outside
some normal subgroup of finite index; equivalently, every non-identity element has a
non-identity image in some finite homomorphic image of $G$. -/
def IsResiduallyFinite (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ g : G, g ≠ 1 → ∃ N : Subgroup G, N.Normal ∧ N.FiniteIndex ∧ g ∉ N

blocks.docstring:
Two groups $G$ and $H$ have the *same set of finite homomorphic images* if every finite
group is a homomorphic image (surjective image) of $G$ if and only if it is a homomorphic
image of $H$. Since every finite group is isomorphic to one in `Type`, quantifying over
finite groups `Q : Type` captures "the same finite quotients up to isomorphism".

justification.closest_existing_considered: No notion of 'is a quotient of' as a relation between groups in Mathlib; MonoidHom + Function.Surjective used directly. Profinite completions do not exist in Mathlib either, so the (equivalent for f.g. groups) formulation via isomorphic profinite completions was not available.
justification.name: Kourovka.«5.48».HasSameFiniteQuotients
justification.why_needed: 'Same set of finite homomorphic images' has no Mathlib counterpart. Defined as: for every finite group Q : Type, (∃ φ : G →* Q, Surjective φ) ↔ (∃ ψ : H →* Q, Surjective ψ). Quantifying over Q in Type is WLOG since every finite group is isomorphic to one in Type, giving 'same finite quotients up to isomorphism'.

blocks.name: HasSameFiniteQuotients
blocks.text:
/-- Two groups $G$ and $H$ have the *same set of finite homomorphic images* if every finite
group is a homomorphic image (surjective image) of $G$ if and only if it is a homomorphic
image of $H$. Since every finite group is isomorphic to one in `Type`, quantifying over
finite groups `Q : Type` captures "the same finite quotients up to isomorphism". -/
def HasSameFiniteQuotients (G H : Type*) [Group G] [Group H] : Prop :=
  ∀ (Q : Type) [Group Q] [Finite Q],
    (∃ φ : G →* Q, Function.Surjective φ) ↔ (∃ ψ : H →* Q, Function.Surjective ψ)

blocks.code:
def IsFreeSolvable (G : Type u) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (α : Type u) (d : ℕ), Nonempty (G ≃* FreeGroup α ⧸ derivedSeries (FreeGroup α) d)
blocks.docstring:
A group $G$ is *free soluble* if it is isomorphic to $F / F^{(d)}$ for some free group
$F$ and some $d \in \mathbb{N}$, where $F^{(d)}$ is the $d$-th term of the derived series
of $F$; that is, $G$ is free in the variety of soluble groups of derived length at most $d$.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Mathlib's IsFreeGroup, FreeGroup, derivedSeries, IsSolvable, FreeAbelianGroup; none captures free soluble groups. Grepped for 'free solvable/soluble', 'FreeSolvable', 'relatively free' — only a doc-comment mention in Mathlib/GroupTheory/Torsion.lean.
justification.name: Kourovka.«5.48».IsFreeSolvable
justification.why_needed: Free soluble groups (F/F^{(d)}, free in the variety of soluble groups of derived length ≤ d) are not in Mathlib or the repo. Defined as ∃ (α : Type u) (d : ℕ), Nonempty (G ≃* FreeGroup α ⧸ derivedSeries (FreeGroup α) d), mirroring the universe convention of Mathlib's IsFreeGroup.

blocks.name: IsFreeSolvable
blocks.text:
/-- A group $G$ is *free soluble* if it is isomorphic to $F / F^{(d)}$ for some free group
$F$ and some $d \in \mathbb{N}$, where $F^{(d)}$ is the $d$-th term of the derived series
of $F$; that is, $G$ is free in the variety of soluble groups of derived length at most $d$. -/
def IsFreeSolvable (G : Type u) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (α : Type u) (d : ℕ), Nonempty (G ≃* FreeGroup α ⧸ derivedSeries (FreeGroup α) d)

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsFreeSolvable.isSolvable {G : Type u} [Group G] (h : IsFreeSolvable G) :
    IsSolvable G := by
  obtain ⟨α, d, ⟨e⟩⟩ := h
  let π : FreeGroup α →* G :=
    e.symm.toMonoidHom.comp (QuotientGroup.mk' (derivedSeries (FreeGroup α) d))
  have hπ : Function.Surjective π :=
    e.symm.surjective.comp (QuotientGroup.mk'_surjective _)
  refine ⟨⟨d, ?_⟩⟩
  rw [← map_derivedSeries_eq hπ, Subgroup.map_eq_bot_iff]
  intro x hx
  simpa [π, QuotientGroup.eq_one_iff] using hx
blocks.docstring: A free soluble group is soluble.

@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«5.48».parts.i : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G H : Type) [Group G] [Group H],
      Group.FG G → Group.FG H → IsResiduallyFinite G → IsResiduallyFinite H →
      HasSameFiniteQuotients G H → IsFreeGroup G → Nonempty (G ≃* H) := by
  sorry
blocks.docstring:
Suppose that $G$ and $H$ are finitely generated residually finite groups having the same set
of finite homomorphic images. Are $G$ and $H$ isomorphic if one of them is a free group?

Here "the same set of finite homomorphic images" means that a finite group is a quotient of
$G$ if and only if it is a quotient of $H$ (up to isomorphism). Since all the other hypotheses
are symmetric in $G$ and $H$, it suffices to assume that $G$ is free; being finitely
generated, it is then free of finite rank (rank $0$, i.e. the trivial group, is allowed).
Free groups are residually finite, but the hypothesis is kept for $G$ as in the original
statement.

claims.decomposer_note: Free-group case (Remeslennikov's profinite-rigidity question): for all finitely generated residually finite G, H such that every finite group is a quotient of G iff it is a quotient of H (equivalently, for f.g. groups, isomorphic profinite completions), if G is free (necessarily of finite rank, rank 0 allowed) then G ≃* H; residual finiteness of the free group is automatic but must still be assumed for H, and 'same finite homomorphic images' is up to isomorphism of the finite quotients.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the same proposition (∀ G H : Type f.g. groups, both residually finite, same finite quotients up to isomorphism (∀ finite Q : Type, G ↠ Q ↔ H ↠ Q), IsFreeGroup G → Nonempty (G ≃* H)), all compile cleanly, and I verified the encoding is faithful: Group.FG + IsFreeGroup gives finite rank with rank 0 allowed; residual finiteness kept on both G and H as in the source; 'one of them' is WLOG G since every other hypothesis is symmetric (symmetry proved as API lemma). c07 chosen as base for its complete bespoke-definition API/test lemmas, repo-conventional theorem name kourovka.«5.48».parts.i inside namespace Kourovka.«5.48» (matching 1_40.lean), and docstrings; light edits to docstrings only.

claims.reviewer_why: Same hypotheses with IsFreeGroup G replaced by IsFreeSolvable G := ∃ (α : Type) (d : ℕ), Nonempty (G ≃* FreeGroup α ⧸ derivedSeries (FreeGroup α) d), i.e. G ≅ F/F^{(d)} (Mathlib derivedSeries: index 0 = ⊤, so F/F^{(d)} has derived length ≤ d, the free group in the variety of soluble groups of derived length ≤ d). import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 5.48

by V. N. Remeslennikov

Suppose that $G$ and $H$ are finitely generated residually finite groups having the same set
of finite homomorphic images. Are $G$ and $H$ isomorphic if one of them is a free
(free soluble) group?

Two finitely generated groups have the same set of finite homomorphic images (up to
isomorphism) if and only if their profinite completions are isomorphic, so the free case asks
whether finitely generated free groups are *profinitely rigid* among finitely generated
residually finite groups. The parenthetical question asks the same with "free" replaced by
"free soluble", i.e. free in the variety of soluble groups of derived length at most $d$
for some $d$.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

universe u

namespace Kourovka.«5.48»

/-- A group $G$ is *residually finite* if every non-identity element of $G$ lies outside
some normal subgroup of finite index; equivalently, every non-identity element has a
non-identity image in some finite homomorphic image of $G$. -/
def IsResiduallyFinite (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ g : G, g ≠ 1 → ∃ N : Subgroup G, N.Normal ∧ N.FiniteIndex ∧ g ∉ N

/-- Two groups $G$ and $H$ have the *same set of finite homomorphic images* if every finite
group is a homomorphic image (surjective image) of $G$ if and only if it is a homomorphic
image of $H$. Since every finite group is isomorphic to one in `Type`, quantifying over
finite groups `Q : Type` captures "the same finite quotients up to isomorphism". -/
def HasSameFiniteQuotients (G H : Type*) [Group G] [Group H] : Prop :=
  ∀ (Q : Type) [Group Q] [Finite Q],
    (∃ φ : G →* Q, Function.Surjective φ) ↔ (∃ ψ : H →* Q, Function.Surjective ψ)

/-- A group $G$ is *free soluble* if it is isomorphic to $F / F^{(d)}$ for some free group
$F$ and some $d \in \mathbb{N}$, where $F^{(d)}$ is the $d$-th term of the derived series
of $F$; that is, $G$ is free in the variety of soluble groups of derived length at most $d$. -/
def IsFreeSolvable (G : Type u) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (α : Type u) (d : ℕ), Nonempty (G ≃* FreeGroup α ⧸ derivedSeries (FreeGroup α) d)

/-- Finite groups are residually finite. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem IsResiduallyFinite.of_finite (G : Type*) [Group G] [Finite G] :
    IsResiduallyFinite G :=
  fun g hg => ⟨⊥, inferInstance, inferInstance, by simpa [Subgroup.mem_bot] using hg⟩

/-- Every group has the same finite homomorphic images as itself. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem HasSameFiniteQuotients.refl (G : Type*) [Group G] : HasSameFiniteQuotients G G :=
  fun _ _ _ => Iff.rfl

/-- Having the same finite homomorphic images is a symmetric relation. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem HasSameFiniteQuotients.symm {G H : Type*} [Group G] [Group H]
    (h : HasSameFiniteQuotients G H) : HasSameFiniteQuotients H G :=
  fun Q _ _ => (h Q).symm

/-- The quotient $F / F^{(d)}$ of a free group $F$ by a term of its derived series is free
soluble. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isFreeSolvable_freeGroup_quotient_derivedSeries (α : Type u) (d : ℕ) :
    IsFreeSolvable (FreeGroup α ⧸ derivedSeries (FreeGroup α) d) :=
  ⟨α, d, ⟨MulEquiv.refl _⟩⟩

/-- A free soluble group is soluble. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsFreeSolvable.isSolvable {G : Type u} [Group G] (h : IsFreeSolvable G) :
    IsSolvable G := by
  obtain ⟨α, d, ⟨e⟩⟩ := h
  let π : FreeGroup α →* G :=
    e.symm.toMonoidHom.comp (QuotientGroup.mk' (derivedSeries (FreeGroup α) d))
  have hπ : Function.Surjective π :=
    e.symm.surjective.comp (QuotientGroup.mk'_surjective _)
  refine ⟨⟨d, ?_⟩⟩
  rw [← map_derivedSeries_eq hπ, Subgroup.map_eq_bot_iff]
  intro x hx
  simpa [π, QuotientGroup.eq_one_iff] using hx

/--
Suppose that $G$ and $H$ are finitely generated residually finite groups having the same set
of finite homomorphic images. Are $G$ and $H$ isomorphic if one of them is a free group?

Here "the same set of finite homomorphic images" means that a finite group is a quotient of
$G$ if and only if it is a quotient of $H$ (up to isomorphism). Since all the other hypotheses
are symmetric in $G$ and $H$, it suffices to assume that $G$ is free; being finitely
generated, it is then free of finite rank (rank $0$, i.e. the trivial group, is allowed).
Free groups are residually finite, but the hypothesis is kept for $G$ as in the original
statement.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«5.48».parts.i : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G H : Type) [Group G] [Group H],
      Group.FG G → Group.FG H → IsResiduallyFinite G → IsResiduallyFinite H →
      HasSameFiniteQuotients G H → IsFreeGroup G → Nonempty (G ≃* H) := by
  sorry

/--
Suppose that $G$ and $H$ are finitely generated residually finite groups having the same set
of finite homomorphic images. Are $G$ and $H$ isomorphic if one of them is a free soluble
group?

Here a free soluble group is a group of the form $F / F^{(d)}$ with $F$ free and $d \in
\mathbb{N}$, i.e. a free group in the variety of soluble groups of derived length at most
$d$; since $G$ is finitely generated, $F$ can be taken of finite rank. Since all the other
hypotheses are symmetric in $G$ and $H$, it suffices to assume that $G$ is free soluble.
Free soluble groups are residually finite (Gruenberg), but the hypothesis is kept for $G$ as
in the original statement.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«5.48».parts.ii : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G H : Type) [Group G] [Group H],
      Group.FG G → Group.FG H → IsResiduallyFinite G → IsResiduallyFinite H →
      HasSameFiniteQuotients G H → IsFreeSolvable G → Nonempty (G ≃* H) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«5.48»

items: 'One of them is a free (free soluble) group' is stated with G as the free / free soluble group; since all other hypotheses are symmetric in G and H (HasSameFiniteQuotients.symm is proved in the file), this is equivalent to the disjunctive reading.
Residual finiteness is assumed for both G and H, exactly as in the source, even though it is automatic for free and free soluble groups.

'Same set of finite homomorphic images' is formalised as: a finite group Q : Type is a surjective image of G iff of H. Restricting Q to universe Type is WLOG (every finite group has an isomorphic copy in Type) and matches 'up to isomorphism of the finite quotients'. The equivalent profinite-completion formulation was not used since Mathlib lacks profinite completions.

IsResiduallyFinite uses the finite-index normal subgroup formulation (∀ g ≠ 1, ∃ N normal of finite index with g ∉ N) rather than the equivalent 'nontrivial image in some finite quotient' formulation.

IsFreeSolvable existentially quantifies the rank (α : Type u) and derived length d ∈ ℕ; d = 0 gives the trivial group, which is harmless and consistent with the free case (rank 0 allowed). Since G is finitely generated in the statement, only finite α can occur.
G, H are taken in universe Type, following the existing Kourovka files (1_40, 19_25, 20_76).

Small API/test lemmas (finite groups are residually finite; refl/symm of HasSameFiniteQuotients; F/F^{(d)} is free soluble; free soluble ⇒ IsSolvable) are included with short proofs, per the CONTRIBUTING.md request for basic API tests of bespoke definitions.

reviewer_notes: No candidate omitted any slot; all eight compiled and agreed on the mathematical content, differing only in packaging (inline vs named definitions; elementwise-finite-quotient vs finite-index-normal-subgroup residual finiteness — equivalent; Fin n vs arbitrary basis type for free soluble — equivalent under Group.FG). Modeling choices in the final file: (1) 'same set of finite homomorphic images' is read as equality of the sets of isomorphism classes of finite quotients, encoded by quantifying over all finite groups Q : Type (WLOG since G, H : Type); the equivalent profinite-completion formulation is unavailable in Mathlib. (2) 'One of them is free (free soluble)' is stated as 'G is free (free soluble)', equivalent to the disjunction by symmetry of the remaining hypotheses. (3) Degenerate cases (rank 0, d = 0, d = 1) are allowed; they are trivially positive instances and do not change the truth value of the universally quantified statement. (4) Residual finiteness is assumed for both G and H as in the source even though it is automatic for free and free soluble groups. Bespoke definitions (IsResiduallyFinite, HasSameFiniteQuotients, IsFreeSolvable) are kept in the problem file, following the existing Kourovka/1_40.lean pattern; a maintainer may prefer moving IsResiduallyFinite to FormalConjecturesForMathlib as a reusable definition. Final file compiles with only the two 'declaration uses sorry' warnings.
statement: Suppose that $G$ and $H$ are finitely generated residually finite groups having the same set of finite homomorphic images. Are $G$ and $H$ isomorphic if one of them is a free (free soluble) group?
